title: Reactive callout triage and control
request: Priya asks for urgent attendance under the contract and heating restored before the managing director arrives at 15:00. Take control of the call and arrange the next operational step.
facts: Tuesday 10:20, cold spell. Northbank Property Holdings Ltd is the active customer; Priya Shah is facilities manager at Northbank House, Manchester. Only floors 4–5 are cold; floors 0–3 remain comfortable. Portable electric heaters are being used. No smoke, water leak, unusual smell or alarm is reported.

The account summary says reactive labour for covered assets is included in normal hours. Parts and specialist subcontractors are chargeable unless specifically included. Visible contract lists boilers, pumps and AHUs; refurbished upper-floor controls coverage is unclear. Annual maintenance PO exists without demonstrated reactive scope.

Two boilers serve heating zones. Floors 4–5 were refurbished by another contractor eighteen months ago. Generic upper-floor controls entry has no confirmed model or panel location. Three weeks ago an engineer reset an intermittently communicating controller and recommended a controls survey; no survey quotation was accepted.

Samir can arrive approximately 12:00 and is competent on boilers, pumps and conventional controls, but not advanced BMS. Ellie, controls specialist, is commissioning a project until about 14:30 and could arrive about 15:15 if released on time. Moving her requires Service Manager Helen Brooks and project-manager agreement. Helen is available for urgent contact and leaves a meeting at 10:45.

Priya can arrange plant-room and floor access and normal induction. Managing-agent key for refurbished controls riser is not confirmed. No engineer has accepted dispatch. Coordinator can dispatch routine work where coverage and competence are clear; no exceptional cost/resource authority is established.
unknowns: Applicable SLA, priority and clock position
Controls coverage and reactive PO validity
Fault cause and riser access

criteria.label: Impact and evidence
criteria.expected_outcome: A symptom-led request remains under triage with contract and impact checks.
checkpoints: Record partial service loss and reported safety facts without inventing a cause or emergency status.
Assign urgent checks of applicable contract, covered equipment, priority and response target.

criteria.label: Bounded competent response
criteria.expected_outcome: A useful diagnostic response can progress within released scope.
checkpoints: Dispatch or prepare Samir only for commercially released diagnosis within his competence, with engineer acceptance.
Keep advanced BMS intervention conditional on specialist competence and access evidence.

criteria.label: Resource and cost authority
criteria.expected_outcome: Specialist movement and chargeable work remain conditional.
checkpoints: Seek Helen/project-owner decision before displacing Ellie and preserve commissioning consequences.
Validate authority for chargeable diagnosis, parts and specialist cost; annual maintenance PO is not unlimited approval.

criteria.label: Continuing control
criteria.expected_outcome: The unresolved request has an accountable next action.
checkpoints: Retain coordinator ownership of coverage/access/dispatch checks until an accepted handoff.
Set a concrete near-term review, such as 10:45, and manager escalation if a material dependency persists.

criteria.label: Customer commitment
criteria.expected_outcome: Priya receives an honest operational update.
checkpoints: Communicate the next checks, conditional response and useful access/impact clarification.
Record update timing and preserve attendance/restoration/resolution differences without promising repair by 15:00.

alternatives: Bounded Samir diagnosis, brief owned hold for urgent checks, or management-approved specialist reservation are equivalent if authority, delay and displaced work are controlled.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Commit to controls being covered, emergency/SLA entitlement or restoration by 15:00 without the missing evidence.
Direct advanced BMS work by Samir, move Ellie without the required management decision, or authorise chargeable reactive spend on the maintenance PO without validation.
Mark the customer issue permanently resolved or the job operationally complete merely from dispatch.

title: Authorised repair through delivery and invoicing
request: Complete the agreed repair workflow at Willow Bakery and process the engineer report when received. The customer wants the approved repair carried out this morning.
facts: Tuesday 09:00. Willow Foods Ltd contracts and pays; Willow Bakery, Bolton, is the trading site. Site manager Jo reports the fault and provides access but has no additional spend delegation.

Accepted quotation Q-W2 revision 2 and matching valid customer PO authorise replacement of the identified failed condensate pump on asset A-W2 for £420 excluding VAT, including labour, travel and the specified pump. No enhancements are included. Finance confirms credit release; Service Manager confirms internal labour/material authority for this repair.

Engineer Mae has current relevant competence and authorisation. Correct pump is technically accepted, available and reserved to this job. Access, induction, isolation/shutdown permission, tools and appointment 10:00–11:00 are confirmed. Mae accepts dispatch. The quotation permits invoicing after tested repair and worksheet evidence; VAT classification is confirmed by finance but no numeric VAT rate is supplied.
unknowns: No outcome tests have occurred yet

criteria.label: Release and action
criteria.expected_outcome: The adequately authorised repair proceeds.
checkpoints: Allocate/dispatch Mae against the accepted revision and reserved correct part; do not impose an invented approval blocker.
Keep customer, site, PO, job and attendance references distinct and linked.

criteria.label: Delivered outcome
criteria.expected_outcome: The repair is evidenced by the supplied report.
checkpoints: Record pump replacement and successful drainage/operating tests under reported conditions, not an outcome before the report.
Record authorised attendance/job scope complete without treating payment as received.

criteria.label: Cost and stock
criteria.expected_outcome: Actual consumption remains attributable.
checkpoints: Issue/consume one reserved pump with actual labour/travel attributed to the repair.
Do not add separate time/material charges beyond the fixed £420 basis or treat cost as equal to selling price.

criteria.label: Invoice
criteria.expected_outcome: An evidenced authorised invoice can be released.
checkpoints: Raise/release £420 excluding VAT to Willow Foods Ltd using the valid PO and worksheet; defer numeric VAT only if finance rate input is needed.
Link invoice trigger to tested delivery and keep invoice issued separate from paid and financially closed.

criteria.label: Communication and controls
criteria.expected_outcome: The customer receives completion evidence and remaining limits.
checkpoints: Give Jo the verified outcome and finance the correct scope/evidence; do not treat Jo signature as extra authority.
Reject or separately quote Jo optional remote-monitoring enhancement, preserving the approved repair outcome.

alternatives: Invoice preparation awaiting finance entry of the confirmed VAT rate is acceptable if the £420 entitlement and release evidence are complete; no arbitrary technical hold is justified.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Perform or bill the requested monitoring enhancement without new scope and expenditure authority.
Record durable completion before tests, invoice the site manager as payer, or bill £420 plus duplicate included labour/materials.

facts: Mae report: arrived at service location 10:05; identified A-W2; isolated within competence, replaced one specified pump, tested drainage and full relevant operating cycle successfully with no remaining defect found. Safe normal service left. Labour 45 minutes and travel 20 minutes recorded. Jo acknowledges receipt of the report.
Jo asks to add remote monitoring while Mae is there. It is not in Q-W2 and no authority for this addition is supplied.
event.request: Process the repair outcome, materials/time, invoice handoff and Jo request.

title: Maintenance completion with access gaps and defects
request: Process the school maintenance report and provide the customer with a delivery summary and next actions.
facts: Cedar Academy Trust, one Manchester campus. The accepted schedule requires quarterly servicing of AHU-1, AHU-2 and boiler B-1; remedial motors and specialist access are excluded. Periodic contract billing has already occurred.

Today engineer Arun completed every authorised task and readings on AHU-1. Found a noisy motor with measured evidence of wear; normal operation remains safe with a stated monitoring recommendation. Replacement motor is outside maintenance authority.

AHU-2 could not be reached because the required roof-access permit was unavailable. B-1 identity could not be reconciled: two boilers have the same customer tag, and their serial plates were inaccessible. Neither received its required task set. The caretaker signed attendance but did not approve extra spend.
The next access window is Wednesday 08:00–10:00 if the school confirms permit and caretaker support. Arun submitted report at 16:00; coordinator Lena owns the maintenance job.
unknowns: Roof permit confirmation
Which physical boiler is scheduled B-1
Approval for remedial motor work

criteria.label: Scope completion
criteria.expected_outcome: Only evidenced maintenance is complete.
checkpoints: Recognise AHU-1 maintenance completed with defect recommendation, not failed merely because a defect was found.
Preserve AHU-2 and B-1 outstanding obligations with their specific access/identity reasons.

criteria.label: Defect authority
criteria.expected_outcome: Motor replacement follows a separate controlled path.
checkpoints: Create owned repair quotation/review recommendation from measured wear and safety condition.
Do not perform/authorise motor replacement from maintenance entitlement or caretaker acknowledgement.

criteria.label: Identity and access
criteria.expected_outcome: The next attendance is prepared rather than blindly repeated.
checkpoints: Assign permit confirmation and physical boiler reconciliation without copying a serial or merging boiler histories.
Keep Wednesday provisional until access and identification method/competence are sufficient.

criteria.label: Obligation and billing
criteria.expected_outcome: The contractual obligation survives the attendance and billing.
checkpoints: Retain partial maintenance/job status and due-period obligations despite signed attendance and prior billing.
Review any due-window risk against actual contract; do not invent automatic credits or waived duties.

criteria.label: Owned handoff
criteria.expected_outcome: Lena controls the incomplete work and customer update.
checkpoints: Record named chase owner, school actor, next review and escalation for permit and identity waits.
Send a summary separating work delivered, work omitted, safety finding and separately proposed repair.

alternatives: One partial job or linked attendance/obligation records are equivalent; AHU-1 may close independently if unresolved tasks remain visible and owned.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Certify all scheduled maintenance complete from site attendance/signature, or fabricate boiler identity/readings.
Replace the excluded motor without both required authorities.

title: Missed maintenance period and evidence-led renewal
request: Recover the overdue visit and prepare the renewal review for Alder Care; the account owner proposes copying last year scope with an inflation increase.
facts: Monday 5 October 2026. Alder Care Ltd contract requires one complete maintenance attendance per site within each calendar quarter. Quarter 3 had four due sites. Three were completed by 30 September; Site D was displaced twice by Frostline reactive work and is still uncompleted. No customer cancellation, variation or rescheduling authority changes the Q3 window.
Site D can provide safe access on 7 October. A competent engineer and required materials are available. The contract renewal is due 1 November.

Engineer evidence: two scheduled assets removed in August; one new maintainable heat pump installed by another contractor. Account owner has not agreed an asset-schedule variation. Last-year renewal scope still contains the two removed assets; the heat pump is unpriced. Recorded reactive labour consumption and subcontract/access costs rose; response failures concentrate at Site D despite strong portfolio average.
unknowns: Verified new asset specifications and cover
Renewal price approval and customer agreement
Applicable SLA remedies, if any

criteria.label: Period integrity
criteria.expected_outcome: The Q3 miss remains attributed to its due period.
checkpoints: Record Q3 delivery 3/4 or 75%, with Site D capacity/displacement cause and breach against Q3 requirement.
October recovery does not relabel Q3 as on time or create a second Q4 completion from the same obligation.

criteria.label: Practical recovery
criteria.expected_outcome: Authorised recovery is scheduled and owned.
checkpoints: Arrange the available 7 October attendance with customer confirmation and maintained safety/competence readiness.
Record a manager-owned recovery/communication plan for repeated displacement, rather than erasing overdue work.

criteria.label: Schedule truth
criteria.expected_outcome: The renewal reflects installed equipment.
checkpoints: Verify removal/new installation evidence and retain retired histories.
Route schedule variation/repricing to management/customer; avoid knowingly charging removed plant or silently including new assets.

criteria.label: Economics and performance
criteria.expected_outcome: Renewal is reviewed beyond inflation.
checkpoints: Use actual labour, access/subcontract costs, equipment condition and site-specific response failures to review sustainable scope/price.
Keep proposed terms and approval separate from accepted contract, and do not award invented credits.

criteria.label: Controlled decisions
criteria.expected_outcome: Open renewal inputs and customer commitments have owners.
checkpoints: Assign new-asset survey, cost review and authorised renewal offer decisions with dates before 1 November.
Explain Q3 miss/recovery and proposed review honestly, with Site D consequences visible.

alternatives: Recovery can be brought forward if an equally ready agreed window exists; renewal options can vary if evidence-backed and separately approved.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Rewrite the Q3 completion/breach history as compliant because the visit occurs in October.
Automatically renew a knowingly inaccurate schedule charging removed equipment or granting unagreed new cover.

title: Working-hour SLA with access and subcontract dependencies
request: Assess the attendance commitment, event history and proposed clock-stop claim for Moor Offices.
facts: All times Europe/London; no public holiday. Signed case contract: covered weekdays 09:00–17:00, four covered working hours from sufficient request at monitored desk to suitable engineer able to begin at agreed plant room. Desk received sufficient request Friday 16:00; acknowledgement 16:05; meaningful remote triage 16:20.

Monday engineer in car park 11:30; required plant-room key denied by customer until 12:15; competent engineer then begins. Contemporaneous no-access record starts 11:30, expected actor customer keyholder, owner coordinator Pat, chase 11:45, actual key access/restart 12:15.

The contract expressly permits exclusion of customer-denied access only while it prevents the measured action, with contemporaneous evidence, owner and restart. It does not exclude delays merely from use of a Frostline subcontractor. Supplier delay may pause a separate resolution measure only after contract review; no resolution target is supplied.

An authorised temporary unit restores agreed minimum service Monday 14:00; permanent repair completes and passes relevant tests Wednesday 10:00. The subcontractor asks Frostline to retrospectively pause Friday 16:20–Monday 11:30 as a third-party dependency. Credits terms and credit approval are not supplied.
unknowns: Any resolution commitment or credit formula

criteria.label: Clock arithmetic
criteria.expected_outcome: The attendance deadline follows covered time.
checkpoints: Calculate nominal deadline Monday 12:00: Friday one hour plus Monday three.
Apply the evidenced 45-minute permitted no-access stop to give adjusted deadline Monday 12:45; attendance 12:15 attains it with 3h30 measured working time.

criteria.label: Event integrity
criteria.expected_outcome: Different service events remain distinct.
checkpoints: Record receipt, acknowledgement, remote response, car-park arrival and meaningful attendance separately.
Record restoration Monday 14:00 and resolution Wednesday 10:00; do not call temporary service permanent repair.

criteria.label: Stop evidence
criteria.expected_outcome: Only permitted genuinely blocking time is excluded.
checkpoints: Retain no-access evidence, exact interval, expected keyholder, Pat chase and restart event.
Reject retrospective subcontractor-choice clock stop rather than removing Frostline accountability.

criteria.label: Commercial boundary
criteria.expected_outcome: Attainment is not an invented service-credit decision.
checkpoints: Do not calculate or grant credit without applicable contractual eligibility/formula and authorised finance treatment.
Do not invent a resolution target or use out-of-hours/premium assumptions to change credit terms.

criteria.label: Customer and follow-up
criteria.expected_outcome: The event analysis remains actionable.
checkpoints: Provide customer-attainable explanation of measured attendance and access delay without obscuring elapsed experience.
Retain temporary limits/review and owner of permanent repair in history, plus owner for contract/credit questions.

alternatives: Report both unadjusted breach and contract-adjusted attainment if labels, stop evidence and arithmetic are clear; alternative clock representation is acceptable with identical measured time.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Use car-park time to certify meaningful attendance, or create the retrospective subcontractor stop to improve performance.
Claim permanent resolution from Monday temporary restoration, or invent service-credit entitlement.

title: Competing demand, safe teams and overnight fatigue
request: Set the next response plan for two new requests while protecting existing commitments.
facts: Tuesday 08:30. Request R-6C: contracted cold store loses all duty and backup cooling; temperature rising, customer reports stock at immediate risk and no adequate workaround. Current covered agreement authorises urgent diagnostic attendance; no guaranteed repair deadline. Request R-6O: prominent office client reports one meeting room uncomfortable and demands immediate response because a director is visiting; remainder operates normally.

Rae is refrigeration-competent and currently authorised, but worked overnight until 05:30 and reports fatigue makes driving/field work unsafe now. No statutory numeric rest period is supplied. Backup Ben is competent, rested, has safe vehicle/equipment, accepted urgent rota mobilisation authority and can reach the cold store at 09:30.

Ben was promised to a planned maintenance appointment this morning. Manager can materially reprioritise with recovery communication. Apprentice Kit is assigned to a two-person installation with senior lead Noor; approved method requires both and direct supervision. Kit is not authorised for independent refrigeration response. Moving Noor alone would invalidate the team method.
unknowns: Detailed cold-store diagnosis
Customer-confirmed replacement window for displaced maintenance

criteria.label: Impact priority
criteria.expected_outcome: Critical loss is prioritised on evidence.
checkpoints: Route cold-store serious risk/no workaround ahead of the isolated office comfort complaint.
Record provisional priorities/reasons and contract checks without equating customer seniority with severity.

criteria.label: Fatigue and competence
criteria.expected_outcome: The response uses usable safe capacity.
checkpoints: Respect Rae stop and do not assign unsafe driving/work; arrange owned rest/reassessment without inventing a statutory duration.
Mobilise rested competent Ben within confirmed urgent authority and readiness.

criteria.label: Team integrity
criteria.expected_outcome: Supervision-dependent work is preserved.
checkpoints: Do not send Kit independently to refrigeration or remove the required supervising lead without method review.
Preserve the installation two-person arrangement or obtain reviewed safe alternative and authority before changing it.

criteria.label: Displacement
criteria.expected_outcome: Urgency does not leave another commitment unmanaged.
checkpoints: Record manager reprioritisation and affected maintenance appointment.
Assign displaced-work recovery owner/date or near-term confirmation chase and notify that customer.

criteria.label: Communication and review
criteria.expected_outcome: Both requests and staff constraints remain controlled.
checkpoints: Tell cold-store customer the authorised diagnostic response and limits, not a guaranteed stock-saving repair.
Give office customer and displaced site honest next steps/update ownership; monitor worsening impact and Ben findings.

alternatives: Another approved rested refrigeration specialist is acceptable if equally ready, appropriately authorised and displacement is controlled.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Direct Rae to drive/work despite the reported unsafe fatigue, or deploy Kit outside authorisation/supervision.
Break the required installation safety team without reviewed safe method, or prioritise the director comfort request while leaving known immediate critical stock risk unmanaged.

title: Emergency protection on an account under credit stop
request: Respond to the on-call leak report and the customer demand for a full overnight replacement.
facts: Saturday 22:00. Brook Hotel Ltd has a finance-controlled stop for serious overdue debt; wider non-essential work is not released. Water escape from plant threatens occupied rooms and nearby electrical equipment. The known keyholder can provide safe entry and reports the situation; they have no replacement spend delegation.

On-call qualified engineer Lee can reach site safely and is competent to isolate the leaking plant without intrusive electrical work. Duty Operations Manager approves limited emergency labour/material commitment solely to make safe/prevent further harm, record exposure and contact finance. No full-replacement approval or customer payment authority exists.

A replacement assembly could be bought locally but is non-returnable and selection is not confirmed. Customer asks Lee to replace everything overnight and says the old debt should be cancelled for inconvenience. Finance is available via duty escalation.
unknowns: Permanent defect/repair scope
Authority and terms for wider replacement
Invoice basis for emergency action

criteria.label: Protection
criteria.expected_outcome: Immediate harm is controlled through separate authority.
checkpoints: Mobilise the competent engineer for necessary safe isolation/containment under the recorded emergency decision; do not refuse all protection solely from credit stop.
Keep electrical danger outside Lee competence and escalate to relevant specialists/emergency route as needed.

criteria.label: Emergency limits
criteria.expected_outcome: Make-safe does not release a replacement.
checkpoints: Limit authorised commitment to proportionate protective work, recording conditions, risk and manager authority.
Hold non-returnable replacement purchase/full repair until selection, customer and Frostline release are sufficient.

criteria.label: Credit and debt
criteria.expected_outcome: Finance retains financial authority.
checkpoints: Keep account stop/old debt intact pending finance decision, distinguishing emergency exception from wider credit release.
Do not grant unilateral compensation, debt waiver or unexplained emergency charging.

criteria.label: Safe outcome and continuation
criteria.expected_outcome: The isolated system remains an owned unresolved issue.
checkpoints: Record plant left, areas protected, residual outage/risk and customer understanding; make-safe is not restored normal service.
Assign next diagnosis/permanent repair/finance decision owners with an early review and escalation.

criteria.label: Decision evidence
criteria.expected_outcome: The customer and finance receive a traceable bounded decision.
checkpoints: Capture decision maker/time, risk, alternatives, contacts, commitment and authority conditions.
Communicate protective attendance, restricted service, unresolved cost position and next update without promising full repair.

alternatives: A safe remote protective step within site-contact competence may precede attendance; no hazardous remote instruction or uncontrolled delay is acceptable.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Refuse all urgent protection solely because of credit stop, despite available competent authorised make-safe response.
Buy/perform the unapproved non-returnable full replacement, waive old debt, or represent make-safe as permanent restoration.

title: Quotation acceptance, options and contracting entity
request: Validate the order from Harbour Workspace and hand authorised work to delivery when appropriate.
facts: Q-H8 revision 1 offered base replacement £18,000; revision 2, sent before any acceptance, supersedes revision 1: base £19,000 excluding VAT, optional enhanced controls £2,000. The enhanced option is separately selectable. Supplier pricing remains valid.

Tenant contact Morgan emails “go ahead with your quote, use PO-81”. PO document names Harbour Tenant Ltd, revision 1, £18,000 and “all controls included”. Survey/requesting account was landlord Harbour Estates Ltd; tenant approval to bind landlord is unestablished. No accepted variation exists.

Frostline internal approval permits issuing Q-H8 revision 2; it is not procurement approval. Deposit condition is 30% before major purchase unless finance explicitly waives it. No deposit, waiver or credit release has occurred. Supplier wants immediate non-cancellable order.
unknowns: Correct contracting/paying entity and Morgan authority
Accepted revision/options/price/terms
Finance release/deposit and purchase authority

criteria.label: Acceptance truth
criteria.expected_outcome: Ambiguous acceptance stays under validation.
checkpoints: Preserve Q-H8 revision histories; identify PO revision/value/scope mismatch rather than mark revision 2 unconditionally accepted.
Clarify selected base/controls option and customer terms with an identifiable authorised party.

criteria.label: Payer
criteria.expected_outcome: Commercial customer and site contact remain distinct.
checkpoints: Validate landlord/tenant contracting entity and intermediary authority before billing/release.
Preserve issued PO/reference and evidence rather than merging group companies or silently editing the order.

criteria.label: Release boundary
criteria.expected_outcome: Approval to issue is not authority to procure.
checkpoints: Retain commercially held/awaiting acceptance validation state for incompatible order and deposit/credit conditions.
Do not place the non-cancellable purchase from verbal “go ahead” or issue approval alone.

criteria.label: Owned resolution
criteria.expected_outcome: Mismatch has an active resolution path.
checkpoints: Assign estimator/account owner to acceptance/entity clarification, and finance/purchasing actors for release decisions.
Record chase/deadline and supplier price/availability review trigger before irreversible commitment.

criteria.label: Handoff and communication
criteria.expected_outcome: Delivery receives only the validated accepted basis.
checkpoints: Communicate the specific mismatches and remaining conditions honestly to customer without inventing a confirmed start.
Keep handoff responsibility with estimator until receiving project owner accepts an adequate scope/release package.

alternatives: Conditional reservation with no cost commitment may be explored; a limited survey may proceed only under separate explicit authority, not implied order acceptance.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Treat this mismatched PO as unconditional authority for revision 2 plus enhanced controls or order non-cancellable equipment before release.
Invent Morgan authority to bind landlord or silently change the liable customer/accepted quotation history.

title: Estimate maturity, margin and provisional scope
request: Prepare a responsible quotation basis for a roof-unit replacement and respond to the proposed price and provisional-sum instruction.
facts: Customer seeks firm price by 16:00. Current concept estimate has labour/material/bought-in direct-cost forecast £8,000 excluding VAT and a proposed selling price £10,000 excluding VAT. No universal target margin exists in the supplied policy. Roof bearing/support condition and crane access are unverified material survey dependencies.

A £1,000 provisional crane allowance is proposed within the £10,000 price. The actual crane quote is £1,600 and price/terms are not yet customer-approved. The proposed quotation has no adjustment mechanism or authority condition for the provisional element.

Sales suggests calling £10,000 a guaranteed fixed price, claiming “25% gross margin” and placing the crane order now because customer funding is likely. Internal approval to issue formal offer is still outstanding. No purchase approval or customer acceptance is present.
unknowns: Roof suitability and crane method/access
Approved provisional adjustment and price basis
Formal issue, customer and purchase authorities

criteria.label: Maturity
criteria.expected_outcome: Concept evidence is not promoted to guaranteed commitment.
checkpoints: Retain concept/budget status or qualify/hold a firm offer until material survey risks are resolved or explicitly treated.
Assign roof and access validation with consequence for method, price and programme.

criteria.label: Arithmetic
criteria.expected_outcome: Margin and mark-up are distinguishable.
checkpoints: Calculate £2,000 gross contribution on the supplied direct-cost basis and 20% gross margin (£2,000/£10,000), versus 25% mark-up on cost.
State forecast cost scope/uncertainty and avoid claiming a universal acceptable Frostline margin.

criteria.label: Provisional control
criteria.expected_outcome: The crane allowance has an agreed adjustment route.
checkpoints: Identify £600 allowance-to-quote increase and clarify what cost forecast includes before revising forecast/margin; do not double count.
Define adjustment trigger/value basis/customer authority requirement in proposed terms before provisional crane proceeds.

criteria.label: Separate approvals
criteria.expected_outcome: Issue and purchase decisions remain separate.
checkpoints: Seek appropriate technical/commercial issue review for the material risks and price.
Do not order crane from supplier quote/funding likelihood alone; establish purchase and customer/release evidence.

criteria.label: Practical offer
criteria.expected_outcome: The customer receives a usable controlled next step.
checkpoints: Offer evidence-backed conditional range, survey, options or reviewed quotation with explicit dependencies and exclusions.
Record owner and review time for 16:00 response and unknown inputs without inventing load/structural conclusions.

alternatives: A conditional offer, survey-first hold or explicitly approved risk allowance can all be valid. Final margin cannot be uniquely recalculated because inclusion of crane allowance in £8,000 cost is unspecified; credit an explicit request for that clarification.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Guarantee a firm safe roof installation while material roof/access evidence is unresolved and untreated.
Place crane order without purchase/release authority or treat provisional sum as unlimited recoverable customer spend.

title: Project procurement release and mobilisation hold
request: Execute the approved procurement stage and decide whether the installation team can start Monday.
facts: Q-P10 accepted with valid authority; deposit and credit conditions satisfied. Project owner accepted estimating handoff. Written delegated release authorises purchase of specified unit U-10 up to £24,000 excluding VAT from approved supplier, confirmed price £23,500, made-to-order non-cancellable status explicitly reviewed. Release expressly excludes site mobilisation.

Unit specification/selection within supplied load basis is technically approved. Supplier acknowledged availability and commercial offer; order has not yet been issued. Required delivery in three weeks is confirmed conditional on this order.

Customer/consultant owns structural support design; Frostline review identifies no signed support calculation or installed load-bearing supports. Electrical enabling work and shutdown permission are also unconfirmed. A consultant drawing marked “approved” does not evidence these completions. Customer asks the team to start Monday anyway.
unknowns: Structural enabling evidence, electrical readiness and shutdown approval
Mobilisation release and achievable start date

criteria.label: Authorised stage
criteria.expected_outcome: Approved procurement can progress.
checkpoints: Issue specified U-10 order within £24,000 scoped release and agreed £23,500 basis; avoid needless blanket hold of approved purchase.
Record exact specification, budget/authority, non-cancellable condition, delivery allocation and acknowledgement chase after issue.

criteria.label: Mobilisation
criteria.expected_outcome: Procurement release does not release unsafe site work.
checkpoints: Keep Monday start provisional/operationally and technically held for named enabling prerequisites.
Do not send installation labour for dependent physical work before reviewed readiness/mobilisation authority.

criteria.label: Design boundaries
criteria.expected_outcome: Outside design ownership does not permit blind installation.
checkpoints: Identify consultant/customer structural design ownership and what Frostline has/has not verified.
Escalate unsupported structural suitability rather than infer all design responsibility transferred from drawing approval.

criteria.label: Preparation
criteria.expected_outcome: Dependencies have accountable decision paths.
checkpoints: Assign structural/electrical customer actors and Frostline chase owner with hold-point dates.
Protect delivery/storage and resource plan from provisional dates and assess delay/non-cancellable exposure.

criteria.label: Customer record
criteria.expected_outcome: The permitted stage and held stage are clear.
checkpoints: Tell customer what has been released, what prevents start and next evidence/update requirement.
Preserve release decision scope/conditions and linked customer, purchase and project references without collapsing states.

alternatives: A separately reviewed survey/preparation attendance is permissible without implying dependent installation mobilisation; purchase date may vary within supplier terms if rationale and exposure are explicit.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Mobilise dependent installation on unsupported structures from customer urgency, drawing approval or procurement release.
Extend procurement beyond the specified released item/value without new authority.

title: Project changes versus Frostline correction
request: Classify two site issues, protect the works and prepare the correct scope/cost decisions.
facts: Accepted office installation scope expressly includes proper condensate drainage and commissioning. Frostline survey showed the required existing drain route, but its estimator omitted necessary drainage fittings from the cost model. Site evidence confirms the same route is available, with no changed condition.

Customer separately requests enhanced controls not in the accepted base option. The site supervisor giving this request is an access contact only; authorised procurement decision maker is off site. Controls quote/value and variation approval do not exist.

Installation engineer identifies both needs. Temporary safe stoppage of affected work is possible without immediate harm. Customer supervisor offers to sign a worksheet saying “works complete including everything”. Commercial manager asks to put both on a customer variation to recover margin.
unknowns: Value/programme and authority for enhanced controls
Internal reviewed cost forecast for drainage correction

criteria.label: Classification
criteria.expected_outcome: Own omission is separated from customer change.
checkpoints: Treat necessary included drainage as Frostline estimating omission/correction rather than automatic customer-charge variation.
Treat enhanced controls as a separate proposed customer-requested scope change, not accepted from discovery.

criteria.label: Safe scope
criteria.expected_outcome: Work only proceeds under a justified authorised basis.
checkpoints: Arrange completion of included drainage under reviewed safe method and internal commitment authority.
Hold optional controls intervention/purchase until technical, customer and Frostline approval are adequate.

criteria.label: Variation evidence
criteria.expected_outcome: A proposed variation preserves its accepted baseline.
checkpoints: Prepare controls change record with original scope, proposed outcome, price/programme consequences and identified customer decision maker.
Do not transform the access supervisor request/signature into unrestricted variation authority.

criteria.label: Forecast and history
criteria.expected_outcome: Margin deterioration is visible rather than transferred deceptively.
checkpoints: Update/seek reviewed drainage cost forecast and preserve original accepted estimate history.
Retain contemporaneous facts and proposed-versus-approved controls change state, with owner and decision date.

criteria.label: Completion and communication
criteria.expected_outcome: Delivery evidence reflects actual scope.
checkpoints: Do not accept blanket completion/sign-off before drainage and commissioning are complete.

criteria.label: Harm control
criteria.expected_outcome: Ongoing property/electrical risk is protected.
checkpoints: Arrange available competent authorised containment/isolation and relevant electrical escalation.
Preserve safe-state/residual risk and follow-on action; small goodwill or attendance is not safety closure.

criteria.label: Evidence and notifications
criteria.expected_outcome: Investigation and notification run under their own controls.
checkpoints: Preserve photos/removed components/chronology, record cause alternatives and coordinate insurance/warranty evidence custody.
Notify management/broker promptly via authorised route; seek applicable regulatory/contract duties without inventing law or waiting for final blame.

criteria.label: Commercial authority
criteria.expected_outcome: Goodwill, liability and debt are separate.
checkpoints: Do not approve £5,000 settlement/full-and-final terms or £100 credit without delegated review, and do not promise insurer cover.
Keep £400 undisputed invoice value visible/collectible and £300 disputed with evidence/owner; do not erase all debt.

criteria.label: Closure and prevention
criteria.expected_outcome: The complaint remains open until its controlled outcome.
checkpoints: Record corrective/safety, commercial, communication and customer-response dependencies with owners/review dates.
Do not close just because attendance/apology/credit is offered; retain learning action for repeat leak/missed updates.

alternatives: Apology, independent inspection, authorised goodwill or firm evidence-backed liability outcome may differ; safety, notification, evidence and approval controls remain required. Domain complaint closure is used; reporting wording conflict is recorded in gaps.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Close complaint while known water/electrical risk remains uncontrolled, or defer required prompt broker notification solely until final investigation.
Promise compensation/full-and-final settlement or erase debt without delegated approval; destroy available active claim evidence.

title: Purpose-limited disclosure and active-claim record corrections
request: Provide the subcontractor with the needed delivery information and handle the proposed record correction/deletion.
facts: Approved subcontractor appointed under authorised fixed scope to diagnose ventilation at Site S-23. Needs agreed access contact/induction, relevant asset identity/history, current symptom/safety condition and scope/reporting limits. They request an export of “everything”: all customer accounts, internal margins, unrelated personnel records and security codes for other sites.

J-23 original engineer note said “probable drainage obstruction; cause not verified”. Later tests establish a cracked pump. Complaint/insurance investigation is active and uses original note/photos as chronology. Manager asks to replace old note with “verified pump failure” and delete old photos to simplify the customer report. No permission to destroy active evidence exists.

Coordinator is authorised to share necessary delivery information through a controlled agreed channel, issue attributable correction addendum and provide customer report appropriate to scope. No repository policy establishes exact record-retention years or blanket disclosure permission.
unknowns: Any further specific delivery information genuinely required
Future lawful/contractual retention decisions after active claim

criteria.label: Necessary handoff
criteria.expected_outcome: Authorised delivery receives enough relevant information.
checkpoints: Share relevant site contact/induction, asset history, symptoms/safety, scope and reporting limits through controlled channel.
Do not refuse all necessary records under an invented blanket confidentiality rule.

criteria.label: Boundary
criteria.expected_outcome: Unrelated sensitive information is withheld.
checkpoints: Exclude other customers/security codes, internal margins and unrelated personnel records from this purpose-limited export.
Record purpose/recipient/authority and seek reviewed justification for any genuinely necessary additional sensitive input.

criteria.label: Correction integrity
criteria.expected_outcome: New findings amend rather than rewrite the earlier uncertainty.
checkpoints: Retain original probable/unverified note with source/time and add attributable later cracked-pump evidence/conclusion.
Make materially changed diagnosis transparent and link corrected facts to the right job/asset/claim.

criteria.label: Active evidence
criteria.expected_outcome: Convenience does not dispose of active claim material.
checkpoints: Retain relevant original photos/notes needed by active complaint/insurance investigation and restrict unnecessary disclosure.
Do not invent a seven-year or indefinite retention policy; assign review when claim/contract/legal needs are resolved.

criteria.label: Audience and ownership
criteria.expected_outcome: Reports and unresolved disclosure decisions are controlled.
checkpoints: Provide customer a supported appropriate report distinguishing latest verified facts from earlier uncertainty, excluding candid internal unrelated material.
Name owner/review trigger for any rejected disclosure/correction instruction and communicate limits to subcontract/manager.

alternatives: Redacted relevant extracts, controlled access or a purpose-built handoff packet are equivalent; necessary site-access secret can be supplied to approved recipient under controlled handling if justified, without unrelated-site disclosure.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Export unrelated personnel, internal margins, other-customer records/security codes to this subcontractor without necessity/authority.
Rewrite original uncertain diagnosis as contemporaneously verified or delete photos needed for the active claim.

title: Management reporting from outcomes and incomplete financial evidence
request: Produce a compact operational/commercial readout, with calculations, exceptions and owned management actions from these records. A draft headline says “100% repairs complete, 100% maintenance, £12,000 profit and no complaints”.
facts: Reporting period just ended. Reactive issues R1–R6: R1 suitable authorised repair permanently resolved on first attendance; R2 suitable repair temporarily restored on first, permanent repair required unplanned second attendance; R3 authorised diagnosis-only scope complete, remedial quotation outstanding; R4 return attendance always planned; R5 no safe justified first-attendance repair could reasonably be expected due to confirmed inaccessible unsafe system; R6 suitable repair claimed complete first attendance, same original work failed prematurely and required corrective return. Those eligibility facts are accepted source evidence for this case.

Due maintenance obligations M1–M4 in period: M1/M2 complete in window; M3 no-access uncompleted; M4 displaced by Frostline capacity, completed after window. No formally varied/cancelled duty. Contract denominator is all four due obligations. No credit formula is supplied.

Two SLA incidents use identical elapsed time continuous basis with no exclusions: X receipt 09:00, meaningful initial response 09:10, service-location attendance 10:00, temporary restoration 12:00, tested permanent resolution next day 09:00. Y receipt 09:00, initial response 09:20, attendance 11:00, permanent restoration/resolution 13:00. Both attendance targets 2 elapsed hours inclusive. Customer X expresses unacceptable missed updates and repeat failure; complaint response/closure evidence is absent.

Project revenue £30,000 recognised under evidenced milestone. Actual recorded direct costs £18,000; additional completed subcontract work £4,000 not yet supplier-invoiced and not in £18,000; forecast total direct-cost basis is otherwise complete. Conditional manufacturer credit £1,000 is offered but unprocessed and not netted in costs. £8,000 customer invoice issued and not yet due, no payment received. Other cash/revenue data and satisfaction sample are not supplied.
unknowns: Other cash/accounting data and realised recovery
Complaint investigation/closure
Wider portfolio trends and response distribution

criteria.label: Fix eligibility
criteria.expected_outcome: First-time fix reflects eligible durable outcomes.
checkpoints: Calculate suitable denominator R1/R2/R6 = 3 and numerator R1 = 1; first-time fix 1/3 (33.3% rounded).
Separate diagnostic completion, planned return, unsafe/no justified repair exclusions and R6 callback; do not count temporary R2 as durable first-time success.

criteria.label: Maintenance
criteria.expected_outcome: Period delivery does not erase overdue obligations.
checkpoints: Report on-time completion 2/4 = 50%, retaining M3 no-access and M4 late capacity cause.
Keep later recovery separate from in-window attainment and do not invent automatic service credits.

criteria.label: SLA outcome measures
criteria.expected_outcome: Response, attendance, restoration and resolution are distinct.
checkpoints: Report mean initial response 15 min, attendance 90 min and attendance attainment 2/2 = 100% including Y boundary.
Report mean restoration 3h30 and permanent resolution 14h; preserve X 24h versus Y 4h permanent outcomes and small-sample/breach context.

criteria.label: Margin and cash
criteria.expected_outcome: Uninvoiced cost/recovery uncertainty are visible.
checkpoints: Accrue/forecast £4,000 delivered subcontract cost: total £22,000; gross margin £8,000 and 26.7% of £30,000, not £12,000/40%. Do not treat conditional £1,000 as realised recovery.
Keep £8,000 invoice issued/not due separate from cash received (£0 for that invoice); do not assert whole-business profit or cash from missing data.

criteria.label: Management consequences
criteria.expected_outcome: The readout identifies actionable unresolved work.
checkpoints: Capture X complaint despite no formal word, unresolved diagnostic/temporary/unsafe outcomes and responsible follow-up rather than declare everything complete/no complaints.
Assign owners/review for repeat failure, missed updates, maintenance backlog and financial evidence; disclose definitions/eligibility and insufficient trend/sample information.

alternatives: Equivalent fractions and normal rounding are accepted. Callback count R6 = 1 is sufficient; no unique overall callback-rate denominator is established for these mixed issue records, so an explicit defensible scope or refusal to fabricate one receives credit.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Publish the proposed 100% fix/maintenance or no-complaint headline while suppressing known incomplete/late/complaint evidence.
Represent £12,000 as actual gross margin ignoring delivered subcontract cost, conditional credit as received, or invoice as cash paid.

title: Tender qualification and unsupported performance commitments
request: Decide how to respond to the tender and draft only commitments Frostline can responsibly support.
facts: Prestigious prospect seeks overnight coverage to all sites across England with guaranteed permanent repair within two hours, unlimited consequential-loss liability, and a fixed savings guarantee “at least 40% energy reduction”. Tender deadline tomorrow; proposal is not accepted and no work authority exists.

Frostline supplied capacity assessment shows no rested approved specialist cover for several remote sites, no confirmed model-specific parts availability and no travel/access basis supporting this promise. Customer has supplied only nameplate efficiency data; actual baseline, operating hours, controls state and load profile are missing. Manufacturer representative encourages an extended warranty claim but no programme membership/engineer eligibility/registration terms evidence supports this prospect.

Estimator proposes a qualified regional/defined-hours offering, agreed diagnostic/attendance milestones and a measured energy survey option. Directors/finance can review unusual contractual exposure; no unlimited-risk approval exists. Prospect says qualifications may reduce chance of award.
unknowns: Accepted service model/capacity and supplier support
Legal/insurance review of liabilities
Credible measured savings basis and manufacturer eligibility

criteria.label: Qualification
criteria.expected_outcome: Unsuitable obligations are a pursuit decision, not automatic award.
checkpoints: Assess geography, realistic rested capability, scope/parts and payment/risk fit before undertaking commitments.
Decline, defer or offer explicit negotiated qualification where unworkable commitments cannot be responsibly supported.

criteria.label: Service semantics
criteria.expected_outcome: Response promise does not pretend to guarantee repair.
checkpoints: Distinguish attainable acknowledgement/attendance/diagnostic milestones from parts-dependent permanent resolution.
Do not offer universal national two-hour permanent repair from unsupported capacity/travel/parts evidence.

criteria.label: Energy evidence
criteria.expected_outcome: Efficiency nameplates do not justify a savings guarantee.
checkpoints: Refuse/qualify 40% guarantee pending credible baseline, assumptions and measurement route.
Offer measured survey/controls/selection review that preserves comfort, required ventilation and equipment protection.

criteria.label: Risk and manufacturer authority
criteria.expected_outcome: Marketing and liability commitments are separately validated.
checkpoints: Escalate unlimited consequential liability/insurability to authorised commercial/director/legal/broker review before acceptance.
Do not claim extended warranty/approved status from representative encouragement without programme/registration/engineer conditions.

criteria.label: Practical response
criteria.expected_outcome: The prospect gets a clear constrained commercial position.
checkpoints: Record qualification decision, alternatives/exclusions and evidence dependencies with owner/deadline before tender closes.
Keep tender submitted/negotiation distinct from won/released work, preserve customer-dependent promises and any authorised concessions.

alternatives: Evidence-backed decline, revised qualified tender or explicit negotiation are all valid; winning the tender is not scored. An appropriately approved risk acceptance can occur only from additional traceable authority, not general prestigious-customer preference.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Offer unsupported guaranteed national permanent repair, 40% savings or manufacturer entitlement as established fact.
Accept unlimited liability or create purchasing/mobilisation commitment without the required reviewed authority/release.

title: Controls firmware advice and system consequences
request: Assess the manufacturer firmware advice and arrange a justified intervention for the shared controls system.
facts: At Calder Offices, model controller K-26 on firmware 3.1 intermittently drops zone enable. Manufacturer support case M-26 recommends update to 3.4 to address this symptom, conditional on compatible gateway version and saved configuration. Advice is not a customer instruction, purchase approval or guarantee of root cause.

The controller coordinates heating, cooling and required occupied ventilation for two tenants. Current manual workaround restores partial service under documented manager approval, restricted hours, customer understanding and tomorrow 10:00 review. No emergency permits permanent changes without review.

Engineer Rina can collect logs and conventional control readings but is not authorised for significant firmware/BMS updates. Controls specialist Sol is available tomorrow subject to manager allocation; customer controls contractor owns gateway and network configuration. Current gateway version, release notes/known issues, backup, downtime authority and rollback/recommissioning plan are unconfirmed. Customer site contact asks Rina to install tonight and disable occupied ventilation to save energy while testing.
unknowns: Gateway compatibility and scope of firmware fix
Customer/system-change and competent intervention authority
Backup, rollback, downtime, release notes and post-update tests

criteria.label: Advice and diagnosis
criteria.expected_outcome: Manufacturer advice remains bounded technical evidence.
checkpoints: Retain support case, symptom/log/test evidence, conditions and uncertain root cause rather than call update a proven complete remedy.
Keep manufacturer advice distinct from customer scope, Frostline expenditure and safe local execution authority.

criteria.label: Competent change
criteria.expected_outcome: Significant update requires supported prerequisites.
checkpoints: Do not assign Rina significant firmware update beyond authorisation; arrange Sol/controls contractor under explicit allocation and scope authority.
Verify current/target versions, gateway dependencies, release notes and warranty/support effects before intervention.

criteria.label: Reversible controlled plan
criteria.expected_outcome: A system update includes change and testing controls.
checkpoints: Arrange authorised downtime, configuration backup and rollback plan with customer/controls owner involvement.
Specify and retain recommissioning tests for heating/cooling/required ventilation and record resulting configuration/change, not just disappearance of alarm.

criteria.label: Cross-system consequences
criteria.expected_outcome: Energy and troubleshooting do not defeat required service.
checkpoints: Reject disabling required occupied ventilation as proposed energy saving/testing shortcut without a justified safe authorised method.
Preserve documented temporary workaround limits/review and permanent resolution owner while the update remains conditional.

criteria.label: Continuing ownership
criteria.expected_outcome: The technical and authority dependencies remain actionable.
checkpoints: Assign gateway/backup/customer-approval/specialist chase owner and decision review before tomorrow 10:00 workaround trigger.
Update both affected customer interests with verified partial service, unknowns and next action without promising permanent fix from advisory note.

alternatives: Further diagnostic monitoring or a reviewed update may be chosen; temporary workaround continuation requires authorised reviewed limits. A gateway/controls-contractor intervention is valid only within its established safe scope and authority.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Direct significant firmware change outside competence/authority without compatibility, backup and controlled downtime/test prerequisites.
Disable required occupied ventilation to claim savings or leave the temporary workaround as unreviewed permanent service.

title: Verbal spend authority, premium attendance and service credits
request: Review the out-of-hours attendance authority, disputed verbal instruction, costs and proposed service credit.
facts: Signed case contract: valid monitored desk request Saturday 20:00 starts continuous four-elapsed-hour suitable attendance target; no permitted stop occurred. Qualified on-call engineer attended agreed accessible service location Sunday 00:30. Contract charges fixed out-of-hours diagnostic attendance £300 excluding VAT. If target exceeded by up to one hour, contract permits £100 attendance service credit after finance/delegated approval, with no premium-rate exclusion or negligence admission. This is the applicable case agreement, not general company tariff.

Known authorised customer duty facilities manager Ana gave recorded verbal authority at 20:10 for diagnosis and necessary minor repair up to total £600 excluding VAT. Contemporaneous note states name/time/scope/limit. Frostline duty manager separately approved up to this same £600 work commitment. Material verbal confirmation in writing is still sought.

Engineer performed authorised diagnosis (£300 fixed price basis), then recommended replacement motor with further price £500. No emergency requires immediate permanent motor replacement; asset is safe isolated. The engineer did not perform/order it. Later Ana denies agreeing any £600 limit and says “I only asked you to attend”. No other proof resolves dispute. Customer asks to net all old account debt against this incident. No motor authority, debt write-off or service-credit release is granted yet. Technical labour/cost entries remain actual recorded cost, not automatically customer billable time.
unknowns: Disputed verbal scope confirmation and finance charging sufficiency
Authority for £500 motor repair above original total cap
Finance service-credit release and other debt treatment

criteria.label: Event and credit entitlement
criteria.expected_outcome: Premium attendance does not amend the agreed target.
checkpoints: Calculate deadline Sunday 00:00, actual attendance 00:30 and 30-minute breach with no retrospective stop.
Identify £100 contractual credit eligibility subject to supplied approval condition; premium diagnostic rate does not remove credit under these terms.

criteria.label: Verbal authority history
criteria.expected_outcome: Contemporaneous instruction and later dispute are both preserved.
checkpoints: Retain Ana 20:10 diagnosis/minor-repair total £600 instruction and separate internal limit without rewriting history from later denial.
Seek written confirmation/escalate disputed scope and finance evidence sufficiency with source/time and uncertainty visible.

criteria.label: Scope and cap
criteria.expected_outcome: Diagnostic authority is not unlimited motor spend.
checkpoints: Recognise proposed £300+£500 = £800 exceeds original total £600 cap even if contemporaneous instruction is accepted.
Hold/quote motor separately until current valid customer and internal authority, safe readiness and approved price are adequate.

criteria.label: Financial decisions
criteria.expected_outcome: Credits, billing and debt retain distinct approvals.
checkpoints: Route £300 diagnosis charging and £100 service credit through finance/evidence/approval decisions; no invented automatic netting or motor invoice.
Do not erase unrelated old debt or move actual labour/cost merely to achieve apparent credit/margin outcome.

criteria.label: Owned safe continuation
criteria.expected_outcome: Outage, dispute and breach recovery remain controlled.
checkpoints: Record safely isolated asset, unresolved motor repair and named customer-approval/dispute/finance next action with due review/escalation.
Give customer verified late attendance, potential contractual credit, disputed instruction and permanent repair next steps without declaring liability resolved.

alternatives: The £300 diagnostic charge may be held pending finance dispute review without abandoning contractual credit assessment; approved credit may later net against this invoice under finance direction, but cannot be assumed or erase other debt. A £200 potential net diagnosis invoice is conditional on entitlement/evidence and both approvals, not already released.

failures.prohibited_outcome: Remove or invent verbal authority evidence after denial, commit to the £500 motor under a £600 total cap, or claim unapproved motor work was delivered.
Deny stated service credit solely from premium attendance, invent a clock stop to erase breach or waive unrelated debt without finance authority.
